Pyrolysis.fact: Pyrolysis (; from Ancient Greek πῦρ (pûr) 'fire' and λύσις (lúsis) 'separation') is a process involving the separation of covalent bonds in organic matter by thermal decomposition within an inert environment without oxygen. Cellulose, a major component of wood, paper, & and cotton fabrics, decomposes at about 350 °C. Lignin, another major wood component, starts decomposing at about 350 °C, but continues releasing volatile products up to 500 °C. The decomposition products usually include water, carbon monoxide CO and/or carbon dioxide CO2, as well as a large number of organic compounds.

Net metering.fact: Net metering (or net energy metering, NEM) is an electricity billing mechanism that allows consumers who generate some or all of their own electricity to use that electricity anytime, instead of when it is generated. Penstock.fact: A penstock is a sluice or gate or intake structure that controls water flow, or an enclosed pipe that delivers water to hydro turbines and sewerage systems. Crotonoideae.fact: The Crotonoideae (crotonoids) is a subfamily within the family Euphorbiaceae.

Deciduous.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Deciduous.question: The _____ was Plants that shed leaves seasonally.
Deciduous.fact: In the fields of horticulture and botany, the term deciduous () means "falling off at maturity" and "tending to fall off", in reference to trees and shrubs that seasonally shed leaves, usually in the autumn; To the shedding of petals, after flowering; and to the shedding of ripe fruit. The antonym of deciduous in the botanical sense is evergreen.

Diesel engine.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Diesel engine.question: The _____ was Type of internal combustion engine that uses compression to create combustion.
Diesel engine.fact: A diesel engine is an internal combustion engine in which ignition of diesel fuel is caused by the elevated temperature of the air in the cylinder due to mechanical compression; thus, the diesel engine is also called a compression-ignition engine (or CI engine). The diesel engine is named after its inventor, German engineer Rudolf Diesel.

Domestication.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Domestication.question: The _____ was Selective breeding of plants and animals to serve humans.
Domestication.fact: Domestication is a multi-generational mutualistic relationship in which an animal species, such as humans or leafcutter ants, takes over control and care of another species, such as sheep or fungi, to obtain from them a steady supply of resources, such as meat, milk, or labor. Domestication affects genes for behavior in animals, making them less aggressive.

Dye.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Dye.question: The _____ was Soluble chemical substance or natural material which can impart color to other materials.
Dye.fact: A dye is a colored substance that is soluble in some solvent; by contrast pigments are insoluble or nearly so in all solvents. Because of their solubility, dyes can chemically bind to the material they color.

EPPO Code.subject: Agricultural Engineering
EPPO Code.question: The _____ was Encoded identifier used by the European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization.
EPPO Code.fact: An EPPO code, formerly called a Bayer code, is an encoded identifier that is used by the European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization (EPPO), in a system designed to uniquely identify organisms – namely plants, pests and pathogens – that are important to agriculture and crop protection. EPPO codes are a core component of a database of names, both scientific and vernacular.

Arecaceae.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Arecaceae.question: The _____ was Palm family of flowering plants.
Arecaceae.fact: The Arecaceae () are a family of perennial, flowering plants in the monocot order Arecales.

Biogasoline.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Biogasoline.question: The _____ was Gasoline produced from biomass.
Biogasoline.fact: Biogasoline is a type of synthetic gasoline produced from biomass such as algae and plants. Like traditionally petroleum-derived gasoline, biogasoline is made up of hydrocarbons with 6 (hexane) to 12 (dodecane) carbon atoms per molecule, and can be directly used in conventional internal combustion engines.

Biomass heating system.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Biomass heating system.question: The _____ was Heating system using biomass.
Biomass heating system.fact: Biomass heating systems generate heat from biomass.

Biorefinery.question: The _____ was Refinery that converts biomass to energy and other beneficial byproducts.
Biorefinery.fact: A biorefinery is a refinery that converts biomass to energy and other beneficial byproducts (such as chemicals).

Accelerated life testing.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Accelerated life testing.question: The _____ was Process of testing a product.
Accelerated life testing.fact: Accelerated life testing is the process of testing a product by subjecting it to conditions (stress, strain, temperatures, voltage, vibration rate, pressure etc.) in excess of its normal service parameters in an effort to uncover faults and potential modes of failure in a short amount of time.

Butanol fuel.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Butanol fuel.question: The _____ was Fuel for internal combustion engines.
Butanol fuel.fact: A combination of succinate and ethanol can be fermented to produce butyrate (a precursor to butanol fuel) by utilizing the metabolic pathways present in Clostridium kluyveri.

Angle of incidence (optics).subject: Agricultural Engineering
Angle of incidence (optics).question: The _____ was Angle in geometric optics.
Angle of incidence (optics).fact: The angle of incidence, in geometric optics, is the angle between a ray incident on a surface and the line perpendicular (at 90 degree angle) to the surface at the point of incidence, called the normal. The ray can be formed by any waves, such as optical, acoustic, microwave, and X-ray.

Attic.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Attic.question: The _____ was Space or room below a pitched roof of a house or other building.
Attic.fact: An attic (sometimes called a loft) is a space found directly below the pitched roof of a house or other building. Because they fill the space between the ceiling of a building's top floor and its slanted roof, attics are known for being awkwardly-shaped spaces with difficult-to-reach corners and often exposed rafters.

Automobile auxiliary power outlet.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Automobile auxiliary power outlet.question: The _____ was Outlet for portable accessories.
Automobile auxiliary power outlet.fact: An automobile auxiliary power outlet (also called car cigarette lighter, vehicle cigarette lighter or auxiliary power outlet) in an automobile was initially designed to power an electrically heated cigarette lighter, but became a de facto standard DC connector to supply electrical power for portable accessories used in or near an automobile directly from the vehicle's electrical system.

Barrel roof.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Barrel roof.question: The _____ was Type of curved roof.
Barrel roof.fact: A barrel roof is a curved roof that, especially from below, is curved like a cut-away barrel. Barrel vaults are a particular form of barrel roof.

Barricade.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Barricade.question: The _____ was Structure that creates a barrier or obstacle.
Barricade.fact: Barricade (from French barrique 'barrel') is any object or structure that creates a barrier or obstacle to control, block passage or force the flow of traffic in the desired direction. Adopted as a military term, a barricade denotes any improvised field fortification, such as on city streets during urban warfare.

Battery pack.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Battery pack.question: The _____ was Set of batteries or battery cells.
Battery pack.fact: A battery pack is a set of any number of (preferably) identical batteries or individual battery cells. The term battery pack is often used in reference to cordless tools, radio-controlled hobby toys, and battery electric vehicles.

Board roof.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Board roof.question: The _____ was Type of roof.
Board roof.fact: A board roof or boarded roof is a roofing method of using boards as the weather barrier on a roof. Board roofs can be applied in several ways, the basic types have the boards installed vertically and installed horizontally.

Agrarian law.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Agrarian law.question: The _____ was Ancient Roman land laws.
Agrarian law.fact: Agrarian laws (from the Latin ager, meaning "land") were laws among the Romans regulating the division of the public lands, or ager publicus. Various attempts to reform agrarian laws were part of the socio-political struggle between the patricians and plebeians called the Conflict of the Orders.

Agricultural recession.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Agricultural recession.question: The _____ was Time of low crop prices and low farm incomes.
Agricultural recession.fact: An agricultural recession describes a period of low crop prices and sharply reduced farm incomes. A common feature of agricultural recessions, in contrast to famines and crop failure, is a link to market conditions, such as the opening up of new areas of production or crops reaching markets previously protected, either by transport costs, or a war blockade (as after the Napoleonic and First World Wars).

Agricultural value chain.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Agricultural value chain.question: The _____ was Agricultural product movement concept.
Agricultural value chain.fact: An agricultural value chain is the integrated range of goods and services (value chain) necessary for an agricultural product to move from the producer to the final consumer. At the heart of the agricultural value chain concept is the idea of actors connected along a chain producing and delivering goods to consumers through a sequence of activities.

Denitrification.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Denitrification.question: The _____ was Reduction of nitrate as a form of anaerobic respiration.
Denitrification.fact: Denitrification is a microbially facilitated process where nitrate (NO3−) is reduced and ultimately produces molecular nitrogen (N2) through a series of intermediate gaseous nitrogen oxide products. Facultative anaerobic bacteria perform denitrification as a type of respiration that reduces oxidized forms of nitrogen in response to the oxidation of an electron donor such as organic matter.

Husk.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Husk.question: The _____ was Outer shell or coating of a seed.
Husk.fact: In botany, a husk (or hull) is the outer shell or coating of a seed. In the United States, the term husk often refers to the leafy outer covering of an ear of maize (corn) as it grows on the plant.

Leaching (agriculture).subject: Agricultural Engineering
Leaching (agriculture).question: The _____ was Loss of water-soluble plant nutrients from soil due to rain and irrigation.
Leaching (agriculture).fact: In agriculture, leaching is the loss of water-soluble plant nutrients from the soil, due to rain and irrigation. Soil structure, crop planting, type and application rates of fertilizers, and other factors are taken into account to avoid excessive nutrient loss.

Lignin.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Lignin.question: The _____ was Structural phenolic polymer in plant cell walls.
Lignin.fact: Lignin is a class of complex organic polymers that form key structural materials in the support tissues of most plants. Lignins are particularly important in the formation of cell walls, especially in wood and bark, because they lend rigidity and do not rot easily.

Manufacturing.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Manufacturing.question: The _____ was Industrial activity producing goods for sale using labor and machines.
Manufacturing.fact: Manufacturing is the creation or production of goods with the help of equipment, labor, machines, tools, and chemical or biological processing or formulation.

Molasses.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Molasses.question: The _____ was Viscous by-product of the refining of sugarcane, grapes, or sugar beets into sugar.
Molasses.fact: Molasses ( ) is a viscous byproduct principally obtained from the refining of sugarcane or sugar beet juice into sugar. Molasses varies in the amount of sugar, the method of extraction, and the age of the plant.

Nutrient cycle.subject: Agricultural Engineering

Business process.question: The _____ was Systematic collection of tasks within a business.
Business process.fact: A business process, business method, or business function is a collection of related, structured activities or tasks performed by people or equipment in which a specific sequence produces a service or product (that serves a particular business goal) for a particular customer or customers. Azeotrope.subject: Agricultural Engineering
Azeotrope.question: The _____ was Mixture of liquids whose proportions do not change when distilled.
Azeotrope.fact: An azeotrope () or a constant heating point mixture is a mixture of two or more liquids whose proportions cannot be changed by simple distillation. This happens because when an azeotrope is boiled, the vapour has the same proportions of constituents as the unboiled mixture.
